newsitem.title: UK: EURO CRUDE OUTLOOK - CONTANGO DEEPENS AS IRAQ FLOWS.
newsitem.headline: EURO CRUDE OUTLOOK - CONTANGO DEEPENS AS IRAQ FLOWS.

text.p: The first shipments of Iraqi crude oil since May, expected later this week, should push European crude markets deeper into contango, traders said.

"If Iraqi crude starts arriving in the Mediterranean and northwest Europe in the second half of the month some of it will have to go into storage. That means the contango will have to deepen," said one.

The Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) said on Monday Iraq planned to export 25-30 million barrels of crude up to September 5, the deadline for the first 90-day period of the six-month oil-for-food deal.
Assuming exports begin on Friday, that means Baghdad will be shipping 1.25-1.30 million barrels per day (bpd) to Atlantic Basin refiners at a time when demand is beginning its seasonal slowdown.
One option is for refiners to store the crude for future use but for that to be profitable, prompt prices have to be sufficiently cheaper than forward oil.

Although cash Brent values lost a lot of ground last week -- the Sep/Oct intermonth spread slid from evens on Monday to -17 cents on Friday -- traders say the discount will have to widen substantially before storage works.
"Brent will continue to fall. We should see Sep/Oct trading at -30/-35 (cents) before long," said a trader for a refinery in northwest Europe.
Dated Brent would also remain pinned back despite tumbling from an 18-cent premium to Sept paper to a 20-cent discount.
"The market will probably go even lower next week. Basically there's very little buying left for August," said one.

Sour Russian Urals would continue to be squeezed by the return of Iraq and could also feel a more modest impact from the first sale of crude oil from Germany's strategic reserves due later this week, traders said.
The first tender for nearly three million barrels organised by the Hamburg EBV agency closes on Tuesday and German refineries like DEA and Veba are the most likely winners.
"Its likely to be pretty poor quality and a relatively small amount but it will displace other barrels," said a trader.
Last week's slide in Dated Brent and the deeper contango, combined with a handful of August cargoes which remain unsold, will pressure other North Sea crudes.
"It looks like a quiet week in prospect but there are a couple of Norwegian grades, particularly Statfjord, which still look vulnerable," said a trader.
North Sea loading programmes for September are due to be released this week and are expected to show little change in volumes with maintenance schedules thin.
Apart from longer term refurbishment at the Brent Delta platform, most of the main British export streams will enjoy a maintenance-free month.
Norwegian crudes like Statfjord and Gullfaks will be in shorter supply, however, with Statfjord B due to close between Aug 25 and Sept 23 and Gullfaks A and B due to close between Aug 28 and Sept 15.
